hints: Notice the conditions for KMnO4 are different, so think about mild oxidation versus vigorous cleavage of the C=C bond.
Cold dilute KMnO4 adds two OH groups across the double bond of but-2-ene to give butane-2,3-diol as product X.
Remember what 2,4-DNPH actually tests for, aldehydes and ketones only, then check if a diol or a carboxylic acid can give that test.
walkthrough:
**Find product X from mild oxidation**

Cold, dilute KMnO4 does syn addition of two OH groups across the C=C bond. It does not break the carbon chain.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3 + [O] + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_3$$
So X is butane-2,3-diol, a diol.

**Find product Y from vigorous oxidation**

Hot, concentrated KMnO4 cleaves the C=C bond completely. Each C of the double bond becomes a carboxylic acid group.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. KMnO}_4} 2\,\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
So Y is ethanoic acid, a carboxylic acid.

**Apply the 2,4-DNPH test rule**

2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine gives an orange precipitate only with carbonyl compounds of the aldehyde and ketone type, with C=O.

Alcohols, diols and carboxylic acids do not react. Therefore neither X (diol) nor Y (carboxylic acid) will react.

options.A: Incorrect. Neither X nor Y contains an aldehyde or ketone C=O group. X is a diol and Y is a carboxylic acid, so neither gives a positive 2,4-DNPH test.
options.B: Correct. X is butane-2,3-diol from mild dihydroxylation and Y is ethanoic acid from oxidative cleavage. Since 2,4-DNPH reacts only with aldehydes and ketones, neither product reacts.
options.C: Incorrect. Students often think the diol will be further oxidised in the test tube or confuse a diol with a carbonyl. X has only C-OH groups, no C=O, so it does not react with 2,4-DNPH.
options.D: Incorrect. Students often think cleavage of an alkene must give aldehydes or ketones. Here cleavage of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ gives ethanoic acid, and carboxylic acids do not react with 2,4-DNPH.
